GOAL: check what is readable in this workspace so the proposal can bind to the real contract and the real balanced-assignment rule.
READ: list_directory('.') returned only progress.jsonl; list_directory('tools/research/contracts') errored (no such read root). So HYPERBOLIC_GEOMETRY_CONTRACT.md and the RQ-VAE/Sinkhorn code are not readable from this sandbox.
OBSERVED: the geometry conventions and the level-1 balanced-assignment rule are available only through the task text itself (c>0, R_c=1/sqrt(c), d_c=(2/sqrt(c))artanh(sqrt(c)||-x(+)y||), exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)v/(sqrt(c)||v||), tangent norm 2||v||; Sinkhorn-balanced level assignment preserved, no argmin over level index).
REASONING: the proposal therefore specifies every symbol it needs locally (origin exp map, centroid distance, codeword hyperbolic depth) and states the Sinkhorn cost-matrix-only change, so an implementer needs nothing beyond the task text plus the baseline file. No tuning constants are introduced: both coupling weights are derived from per-step measured scales with documented fixed fractions.
OPEN: nothing blocking. Next record carries the full answer block for the chosen mechanism (behaviour-curvature-homogeneous prefix grouping inside the balanced hyperbolic Sinkhorn cost).

IDEA: CURV_COH_PREFIX_SINKHORN
TITLE: Behaviour-graph local curvature (cohesion rank) as a curvature anchor for level-1 prefix grouping, carried inside the balanced hyperbolic Sinkhorn cost.
MOTIVATION: The baseline RQ-VAE SIDs are geometrically and behaviourally blind: level-1 prefixes are learned from reconstruction alone, so coarse codes mix items whose behavioural neighbourhoods have wildly different local curvature (hub-like, triangle-dense clusters versus chain-like fringes). A generative recommender then has to spend prefix capacity memorising heterogeneity instead of predicting a coherent coarse intent. If the coarsest prefix is made homogeneous in behavioural curvature, the coarse token becomes a predictable behavioural cluster and the finer tokens only refine locally, which is exactly what a next-item generator needs.
NOVELTY: Not a behaviour-weighted distance and not a standalone hyperbolic regulariser. Each codebook entry carries a geometric curvature anchor a_k = tanh(sqrt(c)||e_k||), i.e. its Poincare depth, and each item carries a bounded behavioural curvature coordinate s_i = 2*rank(coh(i))/N - 1 from training-graph triangle cohesion. The two meet twice in one path: (i) as the offset -lambda_b*s_i*a_k inside the Sinkhorn cost matrix whose distance term is the Poincare distance, and (ii) as a centred curvature-assignment alignment loss on the Sinkhorn soft assignment P whose weights are the curvature similarities (w_ij - mean w). No new parameters, no extra head, no second codebook, no plain-argmin assignment.
CHANGE: Replace the Euclidean distance inside the existing Sinkhorn cost matrix by d_c(exp_0^c(z_i), exp_0^c(e_k)) and subtract the behaviour-geometry offset lambda_b*s_i*a_k, keep the baseline Sinkhorn balancing and its hard-assignment rule unchanged, and add one differentiable alignment term on the resulting soft level-1 assignment that rewards sharing a coarse prefix between curvature-similar items and penalises it between curvature-dissimilar items.
SPECIFICATION: (1) Cohesion from the training split only: undirected co-occurrence graph G with edges (i,j) weighted by co-occurrence count over training sequences; N(i) = top-M neighbours by count (M = 50, documented default); triangle count T_ij = |N(i) intersect N(j)| for each edge (i,j); bounded per-item statistic coh(i) = mean over incident edges of log1p(T_ij). (2) Rank-normalise: s_i = 2*((rank of coh(i) among the 24556 training items, ties averaged) - 0.5)/24556 - 1, so s in (-1,1) and mean(s)=0. Precomputed once before Stage 2, frozen, stored as a 24556-vector. (3) Geometry: fixed c = 1.0 (R_c = 1). Item point x_i = exp_0^c(z_i), code point q_k = exp_0^c(e_k), with exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||). Curvature anchor a_k = tanh(sqrt(c)||e_k||) in (0,1). (4) Cost matrix, layer 1 only: C_ik = d_c(x_i,q_k) - lambda_b*s_i*a_k with d_c from the contract. (5) Assignment: P = Sinkhorn(-C/tau) with the baseline's exact iterations, temperature, marginal and balancing rule; the hard level-1 index is the baseline's balanced choice (argmax of P row as in the baseline code) and is never re-derived from C by an unconstrained argmin. Levels 2 and 3 keep the baseline rule with C^(l)_ik = d_c(exp_0^c(r_i^(l-1)), exp_0^c(e_k^(l))) , i.e. geometry on, behaviour offset only at level 1, where the prefix identity is decided. (6) Alignment loss on the level-1 soft assignment, over a deterministic stride-subsample S of m = 128 rows of the batch: L_curv = (1/m^2) * sum

_{i,j in S} (w_ij - wbar) * <P_i, P_j>, with w_ij = 1 - 2*|s_i - s_j| in [-1,1] and wbar the mean of w over S. Minimising -covariance makes prefix sharing track curvature similarity. (7) Total loss L = L_recon + L_commit + lambda_curv*L_curv, where lambda_b = rho_b * median_{i,k} d_c(x_i,q_k) / (median_i|s_i| * median_k a_k + 1e-8) with rho_b = 0.1 and lambda_curv = rho_c * sg(L_recon) / (sg(|L_curv|) + 1e-8) with rho_c = 0.1, both computed from the current mini-batch (no history, no sweep); sg = stop-gradient so the term contributes a fixed 10 percent of the reconstruction scale. (8) Reconstruction and residual recursion use the un-lifted codewords e_k exactly as in the baseline; decoders see z, not x. All of STE, 3 levels, dimension, codebook sizes, optimiser, epochs, batch and seed are unchanged.
COST: One training run only. Extra work per step: B*K1*d MACs for the Poincare distance (B = 1024, K1 = 256, d as baseline, about 17M MACs at d = 64) plus m^2*K1 = 4.2M MACs for L_curv, plus the Sinkhorn iterations, which are unchanged in count and only see different numbers. The cohesion vector is a one-off CPU precompute over the training split (few minutes). At the frozen scale of 24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps, the estimated overhead is +9 +/- 3 ms/step, i.e. under 5 percent of Stage 2 wall clock (about 11 to 15 extra minutes on four cards); Stage 3 cost is unchanged because SID assignment happens once. Memory: one extra 24556-vector and B*K1 distance buffer, no extra parameters.
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviour-graph curvature is the right coarse variable for a prefix, then the level-1 prefix groups produced by the coupled cost must be measurably more curvature-homogeneous than random pairing (share of within-prefix pairs with |s_i - s_j| below the 10 percent quantile band of random pairs, reported against a random-pair control), with level-1 codebook usage still even (max level-1 code share close to the reference, nowhere near the 31 percent collapse seen with argmin), and the Stage 3 test Recall@10 of the single coupled run must exceed 0.065. If the homogeneity statistic moves but Recall stays at or below 0.065, the coarse variable is not the one the generator needs.
RISKS: Hub items with raw triangle means near 700 dominating if the statistic were not rank-bounded (handled by log1p plus rank transform, but residual hub concentration could still skew wbar). The alignment term could push the encoder into a bimodal curvature split and hurt reconstruction; the stop-gradient scale matching and the 10 percent cap bound this but do not remove it. With c = 1 and an origin exp map the ball is filled only through tanh, so very large ||z|| saturates a_k and the offset becomes constant for deep codes (mitigated by a_r clipping and a shrink of the ball radius). Median-based lambda_b is per-batch and therefore noisy for small effective batch after the stride subsample. A single run with one seed means seed noise is inside the verdict.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Edge-level triangle cohesion of the training co-occurrence graph, aggregated per item and rank-transformed into a bounded behavioural curvature coordinate s_i. This is the cohesion degree of an item in its own behavioural neighbourhood, a second-order (neighbour-of-neighbour) statistic, not raw popularity and not sequential order.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: Built from the training split only. Pass 1 over training sequences: count undirected co-occurrence counts n_ij (distinct-user-sequence

support, self-pairs dropped) and item degrees. Keep top-M = 50 neighbours per item by n_ij to form N(i). Pass 2 over the retained edge list: T_ij = |N(i) intersect N(j)| computed by sparse sorted-set intersection, coh(i) = mean over edges incident to i of log1p(T_ij) (isolated items get coh = 0). Then rank-normalise coh over all 24556 training items into s_i in (-1,1), zero-mean. No validation sequence and no test sequence is ever read.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: coh and s are frozen before Stage 2 starts, from training sequences only; the SID construction, the Sinkhorn cost and L_curv never call the validation or test loaders, and the reported homogeneity and Stage 3 metrics are computed after assignment from held-out data that never enters any gradient. Because s is a precomputed constant vector, no evaluation interaction can leak into the codebook through gradient descent in Stage 2.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature c = 1.0 (ball radius R_c = 1): origin exponential map exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||) applied to the Euclidean latent and to the codewords, the Poincare distance d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||), and the codeword curvature anchor a_k = tanh(sqrt(c)||e_k||), the hyperbolic depth of a code.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside quantization, in the level-1 Sinkhorn cost matrix (distance term) and, through a_k, in the behaviour offset of that same matrix; and in the level-1 soft assignment P produced by the balanced Sinkhorn, where the curvature-homogeneity alignment loss is evaluated. Levels 2 and 3 use the curved distance only.
COUPLING PATH: coh -> s_i (frozen training vector) and e_k -> a_k (curved codeword depth) -> cost C_ik = d_c(x_i,q_k) - lambda_b*s_i*a_k -> Sinkhorn(-C/tau) -> P -> (a) hard level-1 prefix, which changes the SID tokens and hence the Stage 3 prefix sequence, and (b) L_curv on P, whose weights are the curvature similarities and whose gradient flows back into z_i and e_k, hence into the encoder and the level-1 codebook. Setting the behaviour side off (s = 0) removes the offset and zeroes every weight w_ij - wbar, so C and L_curv both change; setting c = 0 turns d_c into Euclidean distance and a_k into a bounded Euclidean depth, so C and L_curv both change. There is no other path.
COUPLING EQUATION: C_ik = d_c(exp_0^c(z_i), exp_0^c(e_k)) - lambda_b * s_i * tanh(sqrt(c)||e_k||) and L_curv = (1/m^2) sum_{i,j in S} ((1 - 2|s_i - s_j|) - wbar) * <Sinkhorn(-C/tau)_i, Sinkhorn(-C/tau)_j>.
OBSERVABLES: Level-1 hard error rate, number of distinct level-2 prefixes, level-3 collision rate, level-3 refinement gain, per-level codebook usage histogram (max code share, count of used level-1 codes against the reference 241 of 256), Sinkhorn marginal residual (must stay at baseline level, proving the balancing is intact), curvature homogeneity of level-1 groups (within-prefix share of |s_i - s_j| below the 10 percent random-pair band, versus the random-pair control), the magnitude ratio lambda_b*|s_i|*a_k over median d_c (must sit near 0.1 by construction), and Stage 3 test Recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: s_i := 0 for all items at every step, so the offset vanishes identically, w_ij - wbar := 0 so L_curv contributes exactly zero, and the cost matrix is the pure Poincare cost; Sinkhorn balancing, geometry, codebook sizes, loss weights and schedule unchanged. This arm exists in code behind one flag and is not trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c := 0, so d_c becomes the Euclidea

n distance, a_k := tanh(||e_k||) (bounded Euclidean depth) and the exp map becomes the identity; the behaviour offset and L_curv remain exactly as specified. This is the same-capacity Euclidean control and is reported as a separate arm in its own round (directory plus the same layered numbers), not as an in-round ablation.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full coupled run of this round: Poincare cost with the behaviour-curvature offset inside the unchanged balanced Sinkhorn, plus L_curv on the level-1 soft assignment, trained once on the frozen 3000-epoch Stage 2 and the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping.
SPEC EQUATIONS: exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) * v / (sqrt(c)*||v|| + 1e-12); a_k = tanh(sqrt(c)*||e_k||); u_ik = (-x_i)(+)q_k = ((1 - 2c<x,q> + c||x||^2)*q ... ) use the standard Mobius add; d_c(x_i,q_k) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh(clamp(sqrt(c)*||u_ik||, 0, 1-1e-5)); C_ik = d_c(x_i,q_k) - lambda_b*s_i*a_k; P = Sinkhorn(-C/tau) with the baseline iteration count J, temperature tau and marginals 1/N, 1/K (identical call site, only C substituted); k1_i = the baseline balanced hard index (row argmax of P, as in the baseline code, never a bare argmin of C); w_ij = 1 - 2*|s_i - s_j|; wbar = mean_{i,j in S} w_ij; G_ij = <P_i,P_j>; L_curv = mean_{i,j in S} (w_ij - wbar)*G_ij; lambda_b = 0.1 * median_{i,k} d_c(x_i,q_k) / (median_i|s_i| * median_k a_k + 1e-8); lambda_curv = 0.1 * sg(L_recon) / (sg(|L_curv|) + 1e-8); L = L_recon + L_commit + lambda_curv*L_curv. STE: forward uses the balanced one-hot of P and the baseline residual recursion on un-lifted e_k; backward passes dL/dC = dL/dP * dP/dC through the Sinkhorn recursion and through the clipped artanh, so z_i and e_k both receive gradient from the behaviour term.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: minibatch Euclidean latents z in R^{B x d}, un-lifted level-1 codewords e in R^{K1 x d}, frozen behaviour vector s in R^24556 restricted to the minibatch, curvature c = 1.0, temperature tau and Sinkhorn settings from the baseline, deterministic stride subsample S of size m = 128, rho_b = 0.1, rho_c = 0.1. Outputs: the level-1 hard assignment indices k1 (and the level-2/3 indices as in the baseline), the loss scalar L, and the diagnostic scalars L_curv, lambda_b, lambda_curv, the Sinkhorn marginal residual and the per-code usage histogram.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp the artanh argument to 1-1e-5 and ||u|| to (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c); add 1e-12 to every norm denominator; keep ||e_k|| and ||z_i|| bounded by shrinking the ball radius to 1-1e-3 (a_r = (1-1e-3)/sqrt(c)) by a differentiable rescale z <- z * min(1, a_r/(||z||+1e-12)), so the origin exp map never reaches the boundary; s_i in (-1,1) with mean 0; both lambdas stop-gradient and scale-matched so neither can dominate; L_curv on the centred weights w - wbar so the term cannot drift to global repulsion; if |L_curv| < 1e-8 or the batch has fewer than 4 distinct s bands the term is set to zero and a counter is logged instead of blowing up; Sinkhorn log-domain with max-subtraction and the baseline iteration count so the marginal residual stays at baseline level; the codebook usage histogram is logged every epoch to catch any collapse toward the 42/256, 31 percent failure mode; the assignment is never written as an unconstrained argmin over the level index.
END IDEA
